name: Design Lounge
license: Free to use in products. Credit appreciated. Do not republish as a catalogue.
readme: Read this first. Then open only what you lock: starts/<id>.json for the recipe, themes/<id>.css, pairings/<id>.css, and briefs/<id>.md for each piece. Search pieces.txt for pieces. Do not read index.json; it is the whole catalogue for tools.

kinds.title: A public website
kinds.blurb: Marketing, studio, or company site. Heroes, proof, a footer that signs off.
kinds.when: People arrive from the outside. The first viewport has to hold them.

kinds.title: A product or service
kinds.blurb: SaaS, a tool, a service with a price. Data when it earns the screen.
kinds.when: Someone is deciding whether to use you. Clarity over theatre.

kinds.title: A company platform
kinds.blurb: The thing staff live in: ops, admin, a dense home. Density without noise.
kinds.when: People open this every morning. Taste has to survive eight hours.

kinds.title: A personal app
kinds.blurb: One person’s money, health, or home. Not a staff tool, and not a marketing site.
kinds.when: The person using it is the customer. The number on the screen is theirs.

families.name: Quiet
families.mood: Hairlines, 6px corners, one solid button. The safe default for products that have to last.
rules: Radius 6px on controls, 8px on cards. Never more.
One solid primary. Secondary is outline, same height (40px web / 44px phone).
Hairline borders at 1px. No drop shadows on tables.
Focus ring 2px accent, 3px offset.

families.name: Soft
families.mood: Tonal fills, 14px corners, pills. Friendly without becoming a toy.
rules: Radius 14px on cards, 999px on chips and the primary button.
Primary is a soft accent wash, not a hard fill, unless contrast needs it.
Plenty of air: 24px gaps, 20px card pad.
Phone targets 44px. No hairlines thinner than 1px.

families.name: Sharp
families.mood: Zero radius, visible grid, type that does the work. Swiss without the poster shout.
rules: Radius 0 everywhere. If you round a button you have left the family.
1px ink rules. No shadows. Alignment is the decoration.
Primary can be a solid ink block; hover inverts.
Uppercase 11px labels, 0.12em tracking, on data and nav.

families.name: Editorial
families.mood: Paper, measure, a serif that holds a room. Buttons stay quiet so the type can speak.
rules: Measure 58–66ch on reading. Headlines can break the grid.
Buttons are outlined, 40px, no fill until hover.
Paper grain or warm off-white is allowed; stock photos are not.
Italic is a voice, used once per viewport.

families.name: Glass
families.mood: Translucent bars, 16px corners, things that float. Native feel on the web.
rules: Bars use backdrop-filter: blur(16px) at ~72% opacity. Always give a solid fallback.
Radius 16px on sheets, 999px on tab pills.
Phone chrome: 44px tab bar, home indicator clearance 10px.
Do not glass a whole page. One floating layer is enough, unless a Named aesthetic (glassmorphism) lifts that; then surfaces may frost over one image or scene layer.

families.name: Industrial
families.mood: Utility first. Tight type, 2px corners, labels that read like a yard sheet.
rules: Radius 2px. Dense padding (12px). Tables are first-class.
Primary is a committed fill (accent or ink). 36px on web, 44px on phone.
Mono for numbers. Tabular nums. No ornament.
Status colour is reserved for live state, never decoration.

families.name: Bold
families.mood: Neo-brutalism. A 2px ink border on everything, a hard offset shadow, flat bright fills. Loud, square, nothing blurred.
rules: Radius 0 to 6px: 4px on controls, 6px on cards, 0 on a hero block or a sticker. Never a pill.
Every card and control has a 2px border in --ink. The offset shadow is the family shadow: 4px 4px 0 var(--ink), no blur, no alpha. A hero card may take 8px 8px 0.
Hover moves the element into its shadow: translate(4px, 4px) while the shadow collapses to 0, both on one 120ms clock. Nothing lifts.
Fills are flat: --surface, --primary, --secondary, --tertiary. No gradient, no tint, no blur. Ink is --ink, never pure #000.

families.name: Tactile
families.mood: Clay and neumorphism. One surface colour, light from the top left, controls raised out of it or pressed into it. Soft and round, and still readable.
rules: Radius 18 to 24px on cards and controls. 999px only on a knob, a switch, or a round transport button.

Two shadow tokens, both built from the theme surface: --raise for a control at rest (light top-left, shade bottom-right, outside) and --well for a pressed, inset, or track state (the same pair, inset). Never a drop shadow in a third colour, and never a shadow on --bg that differs from --surface.
Every control keeps 3:1 non-text contrast against the surface: a 1px edge at --line-strong, or a fill in --primary-soft, on top of the shadow. The shadow alone is decoration, not the boundary.
A pressed or on state is the inset shadow plus --primary (or --ink in a monochrome theme) on the icon, knob, or label, so the change is visible without the depth.

families.name: Lit
families.mood: A scene or an object with real light: glow, depth, atmosphere. The interface floats over it in pills and hairlines.
rules: The drawn scene or object gets light: layered radial gradients, glow, a highlight edge, a cast shadow, grain. Flat fills only on the interface.
Controls are 999px pills with a 1px line at 12-20% ink. One filled primary.
The display face runs huge (10-16vw) with one word in italic or in the light colour.
Small mono readouts are allowed when they are live and belong to the idea: a clock, a distance, a countdown. Never more than four on screen.

starts.title: Real estate
starts.when: A property listing, an agent, or a rental site. Marble Hall for a high price, Fog City for city rentals.

starts.title: A restaurant
starts.when: A restaurant, a cafe, or a bar people visit. Not a food shop that ships; that is food.

starts.title: A school or course
starts.when: An online course, a school, a college, or a bootcamp.

starts.title: A job board
starts.when: A job board, a careers page with many roles, or a hiring marketplace.

starts.title: A nonprofit
starts.when: A charity, a fundraiser, or a community group asking for money or time.

starts.title: A clinic
starts.when: A dental, physio, vet, or doctor clinic people book. A retreat is wellness.

starts.title: A gym
starts.when: A gym, a boxing club, a yoga or spin studio with a timetable.

starts.title: A firm
starts.when: A law firm, an accountant, a consultant, or an advisory practice.

starts.title: A marketing site
starts.when: A company, studio or product needs a public website with a point of view — not a template.

starts.title: A SaaS site
starts.when: A software product needs a public page. Fog City, because this is SaaS. Atelier Noir is a fashion room, so it loses.

starts.title: A portfolio
starts.when: A visual designer, photographer, architect, or studio whose work is images. Someone who ships software takes portfolio-builder instead.

starts.title: A builder’s portfolio
starts.when: A developer, product manager, product designer, or founder. Kiln, warm and light, because the work is the colour. Atelier Noir is a fashion room, so it loses.

starts.title: Fintech
starts.when: Banking, payments, or a ledger someone is deciding to trust.

starts.title: Fashion
starts.when: Clothes, fragrance, or a luxury good. Linen and a Didone, not a product sans.

starts.title: A food shop
starts.when: A kitchen, a stall, or a menu people order from.

starts.title: Wellness
starts.when: A retreat, a studio class, or a clinic people book. Alpine Clinic, because this is a body. Loam is the food shop, so it loses.

starts.title: A hotel
starts.when: A hotel, a house, or a night people reserve.

starts.title: An agency
starts.when: A studio selling the work, after dark.

starts.title: Documentation
starts.when: A guide, an API, or a changelog people keep open.

starts.title: A music site
starts.when: A label, a release, or a night. Neon, not a paper magazine.

starts.title: A personal site
starts.when: A person, not a studio. The writing is the work.

starts.title: An event
starts.when: A festival, a launch night, or a programme with hours.

starts.title: A museum
starts.when: A gallery, a collection, or a room people walk.

starts.title: A landing page
starts.when: A launch, a waitlist, or one product page, including a tilt, a sticky scroll, or a hover on the product.

starts.title: A mobile app
starts.when: A phone product that should feel shipped, not like a website squeezed into 390px. Motion on a phone is a native piece, not a cursor.

starts.title: A design system
starts.when: A new product needs a grammar — tokens and taste — before components.

starts.title: A dashboard
starts.when: An internal tool, analytics home, or ops screen people will live in all day.

starts.title: A web app
starts.when: The app itself, in a browser. Not the marketing site (that is saas) and not a staff dashboard.

starts.title: A shop
starts.when: A product, a bowl, a kit — something people buy without a carnival.

starts.title: A tablet
starts.when: Someone holds the product in two hands. The frame is 1180 wide, and a phone list does not belong there.

starts.title: An editorial product
starts.when: A magazine, a journal, a long-read product where the type is the design.

starts.title: A bank app
starts.when: A phone someone opens to see their money. Not the staff ledger.

starts.title: A health app
starts.when: Fitness, a clinic, or a body people check daily.

starts.title: Messages
starts.when: Chat, mail, or a list of conversations.

starts.title: A music app
starts.when: A song, a queue, a night. The player is the product.

starts.title: A news app
starts.when: News or a magazine someone reads on a phone.

starts.title: A shop app
starts.when: Buying on a phone. The bag is the next screen, not a carnival.

starts.title: A social app
starts.when: People, posts, or stories. One feed, not a dashboard.

starts.title: Weather
starts.when: A forecast. One place, the next hours, nothing else.

starts.title: A field app
starts.when: Staff on a phone, outside. A yard, a route, a job.

starts.title: A personal app
starts.when: Money, health, or home for the person using it. A Nepali finance app starts here.

starts.title: A game
starts.when: A game site: arcade, a small web game, a card table, a lobby, or a 3D scene. Not a marketing page with a Play button that goes nowhere.

starts.title: A handwritten site
starts.when: A personal site, a cafe, a workshop, or a letter. Notes in the margin of a normal site use Handwritten Notes instead.

pairings.name: Gallery Wall
pairings.mood: Quiet confidence. A serif with ink-trap italics over a neutral grotesk.

pairings.name: The Lounge
pairings.mood: Warm, literary, a little soft. The house pairing of this site.

pairings.name: Newsroom
pairings.mood: Serious reporting with a friendly sans for the furniture.

pairings.name: Swiss Precision
pairings.mood: Grid-first. Tight grotesk, mono for data and captions.

pairings.name: Brutal Grotesk
pairings.mood: Loud headlines, plain body, nothing in between.

pairings.name: Maison
pairings.mood: High-contrast Didone with an airy humanist. Restraint as luxury.

pairings.name: Studio Display
pairings.mood: Art-school geometry with a calm, readable companion.

pairings.name: Developer Docs
pairings.mood: Neutral, technical, legible at 13px. Built for code next to prose.

pairings.name: Bookish
pairings.mood: Old-style serif reading comfort with a friendly grotesk for UI.

pairings.name: Poster Condensed
pairings.mood: Tall and urgent. Condensed caps with a mono to keep it honest.

pairings.name: Deco Hotel
pairings.mood: Thin, tall, 1920s. Geometric sans for the room numbers.

pairings.name: Atelier
pairings.mood: A heavy display serif with a soft, rounded geometric for everything else.

pairings.name: Arcade
pairings.mood: Bitmap caps over a mono body. Insert coin.
pairings.caution: Body text is Space Mono on purpose. Keep it for the game. Do not use this pairing for reports or long prose.

pairings.name: HUD
pairings.mood: Angular, technical, cockpit-adjacent. Pairs with cut corners and scanlines.
pairings.caution: Body text is Share Tech Mono on purpose. Cockpit and status screens only. Do not use it for reports.

pairings.name: Candy Clay
pairings.mood: Puffy, round, delighted. Built for chunky buttons.

pairings.name: Friendly SaaS
pairings.mood: Modern product sans with a mono for numbers and keys.

pairings.name: Devanagari
pairings.mood: A Nepali display serif for headings and amounts. Mukta for the interface. The currency word and the digits share one face.
pairings.caution: IBM Plex Mono is for Latin codes only. An amount that contains रु, रू, or Devanagari digits is set entirely in Noto Serif Devanagari or Mukta, digits included. Do not let the currency word fall back to another face. Group Nepal and India digits by lakh: 1,24,000.

pairings.name: Bauhaus School
pairings.mood: Geometric heavyweight with a mono for the rules.

pairings.name: Wide Tech
pairings.mood: Extended display, crisp neutral body. Feels engineered and expensive.

pairings.name: Garden Journal
pairings.mood: Chunky friendly serif, generous grotesk. Earthy and kind.

pairings.name: Literary
pairings.mood: Calligraphic Garamond display with a quiet sans for UI.

pairings.name: Riso Zine
pairings.mood: Monoline heavyweight caps and its own family for body. Photocopied joy.

pairings.name: Industrial Label
pairings.mood: Tall stencil-adjacent caps and a workhorse sans.

pairings.name: Letter Hand
pairings.mood: The whole site is handwritten. A loose script for titles, a clear printed hand for everything you read.
pairings.caution: Body text is Patrick Hand. Do not set paragraphs in Gochi Hand, Caveat, or a signature script. Keep lines short. Do not use this pairing for a dashboard, a game, or a form-heavy tool.

pairings.name: Handwritten Notes
pairings.mood: A real hand for annotations, a neutral grotesk for the rest.
pairings.caution: Only the notes are handwritten. Buttons, nav, and paragraphs stay in the sans. For a site that is entirely handwritten, use Letter Hand.

pairings.name: Slab Ledger
